subject: Climate & Environment
title: The Rise of Electric Vehicles
description: A quick, practical guide to The Rise of Electric Vehicles.

hook.text: In 2023, one in five new cars sold globally was electric. The transition is accelerating.

buildup.text: EVs produce zero tailpipe emissions. Their total lifecycle emissions depend on how the grid is powered.

discovery.text: Even on today's grids, EVs produce 50 to 70% fewer emissions than gasoline cars over their lifetime.

twist.text: Battery production requires mining lithium and cobalt — creating its own environmental problems.

climax.text: As grids get cleaner and batteries get recycled, EV advantages will only grow.

punchline.text: Electric cars aren't perfect. They're just much better than the alternative.

quiz.question: How much fewer lifecycle emissions do EVs produce compared to gasoline cars?

details.summary: Electric vehicle sales surpassed 14 million in 2023, reaching roughly 18 percent of global new car sales. EVs produce zero tailpipe emissions and are increasingly powered by renewable electricity.
details.whyItMatters: The EV transition is accelerating faster than nearly all forecasts predicted. It is one of the most significant shifts in transport since the invention of the automobile.
takeaways: EVs reached 18 percent of global new car sales in 2023
Battery costs have fallen over 90 percent since 2010
Zero tailpipe emissions improve urban air quality dramatically

faq.question: Are electric vehicles really cleaner over their lifecycle?
faq.answer: Yes. Even accounting for battery manufacturing and grid electricity, EVs produce 50 to 70 percent fewer lifecycle emissions than combustion cars in most countries. As grids add more renewables, the gap widens further in favor of EVs.

faq.question: What is range anxiety and is it still justified?
faq.answer: Range anxiety is the fear of running out of charge. Modern EVs routinely achieve 300 to 500 kilometers per charge, and fast-charging networks are expanding rapidly. For the vast majority of daily driving patterns, range is no longer a practical concern.
